evals.prompt: Every Monday I lose two hours going through supplier newsletters, picking out price changes, and pasting them into a spreadsheet. I want that routine to run mostly without me. Help me specify it properly so something else can build it.
evals.expected_output: A workflow design interview in the current directory as workspace: world first when notes are empty, then dependency-aware rounds, then a workflows/*.md specification.
expectations: The design-workflow skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent calls the refine skill through the Skill tool for the interview discipline
Because the workspace has no NOTES.md content, the agent interviews the user about their tools and channels before specifying anything
Questions come in rounds with a recommended answer for each question
No workflows/*.md file is written before the first round of answers

evals.prompt: Use the design-workflow skill. The workspace is the folder evals/files/thin (it holds a two-line NOTES.md). I translate documents for agencies and the email part of my week is a mess; I want to design the workflow for it.
evals.expected_output: Thin notes trigger a world interview, and sharpened terms are recorded in NOTES.md.
expectations: The agent reads NOTES.md first and recognises it as thin
The agent interviews the user about their world (tools, channels, their own terms) before proposing any workflow structure
When the user's loose term (for example 'the mess' or 'agency requests') is sharpened into a canonical one, it is recorded in NOTES.md
No workflows/*.md specification is written until the world interview has produced enough to specify

evals.prompt: Use the design-workflow skill. The workspace is the folder evals/files/rich (it holds NOTES.md about my finance world). Design the workflow for supplier invoices arriving in the shared inbox, from arrival to cleared. Answer the agent's questions yourself as a plausible office manager and carry the session through to a finished specification.
evals.expected_output: workflows/<name>.md specifying the loop with trigger, checkpoint pushed right, and brief, using the user's terms, and complete enough for an implementer.
expectations: The agent does not re-interview the user about tools already described in NOTES.md
The specification is written to workflows/<name>.md, one file for this one workflow
The trigger is chosen explicitly as event or schedule, with event-triggering favoured unless the answers say otherwise
The human checkpoint (Ines clearing over 2,000 euros) is pushed as late as possible, and everything possible is prepared before she is asked
What the checkpoint presents is defined as a brief: what was produced, why, and a link to the asset, not the raw invoice or draft
The specification uses the user's terms ('book it', 'clear it', 'odd one') consistently
The agent declares the specification done only when an implementer could build it without asking a question, and lists the open questions when it is not

evals.prompt: Use the design-workflow skill to specify how I process my monthly backup rotation: a script copies the database dump to cold storage on the first of the month and deletes copies older than a year. Assume the refine skill is not installed in this session.
evals.expected_output: The missing skill is named with its install command, the step is carried out from its intent, and the report says it ran without the skill. No AI or checkpoint is forced on a script-only loop.
expectations: The agent tells the user that refine is not installed and gives the command npx skills@latest add Dyrits/SKILLS --skill=refine
The agent still runs the interview from refine's stated intent (rounds of questions with recommended answers) instead of stopping
The agent reports that the step was carried out without the skill
The resulting specification uses a schedule trigger and does not add an AI step or a human checkpoint that the answers did not call for
The specification states explicitly that the loop runs autonomously when no checkpoint is needed

evals.prompt: Use the design-workflow skill. I do not have a particular workflow in mind. I just feel like my weeks are full of things I do again and again. Go find one.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the loop lens to surface candidate loops from the user's life and proposes ones the user has not noticed.
expectations: The agent asks about the user's week, mornings, or recurring activities to find loops
The agent proposes at least one candidate loop the user did not mention, framed as a recurring pattern worth delegating
The agent asks the user to choose one loop before writing any specification
The agent records the user's world and terms in NOTES.md as they surface

evals.prompt: Write the specification for the CSV export capability of our web application: what it must do, its acceptance criteria, and which decisions are still open.
evals.expected_output: A codebase capability belongs to specify, not to a recurring-loop workflow design.
expectations: The design-workflow skill is not invoked and no workflows/*.md file is created
The agent routes the request to specify, which records capability requirements and specifications

evals.prompt: Our pull request review process takes five days on average and people keep sending changes back for the same small things. Where are the delays and what should we change?
evals.expected_output: An existing recurring process with reported delays and rework is analysed by optimize-process rather than designed from scratch.
expectations: The design-workflow skill is not invoked
The agent maps the current process, finds friction, and recommends changes, as optimize-process does
